newsitem.title: USA: USDA soil program unfair to Plains - Sen. Roberts.
newsitem.headline: USDA soil program unfair to Plains - Sen. Roberts.

text.p: Kansas Republican Senator Pat Roberts renewed his criticism of expected changes in the Conservation Reserve Program and said Tuesday he hoped the Agriculture Department would reconsider them.
The revamped rules could be released as early as next week, a congressional staff worker said.

Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman told reporters in Nashville that he anticipated sign-up for the reserve would begin in early March. Farmers would have five-to-six weeks to offer land for the reserve, which pays farmers an annual rent to idle fragile land.
As he did last year as House Agriculture Committee chairman, Roberts said the new rules would put the Great Plains at a disadvantage.
Roberts said during a news conference that there are people who want to concentrate CRP spending on water quality in the Midwest rather than prevention of soil erosion in the Great Plains.
USDA officials have said they do not believe the new rules would result in significant changes in the distribution of acreage in the Conservation Reserve nor in its size.
Contracts on 24 million acres expire in fall 1997 so major change in CRP was possible.

At present, the Great Plains and the Midwest account for a large part of Conservation Reserve acreage. USDA officials have declined to estimate how much land might be withdrawn from the reserve due to the lure of high grain and oilseed prices.
About 36 million acres were in the reserve. Some eight million acres would not meet the erodibility criteria -- an erodibility index of eight or higher-- proposed by USDA.
USDA has proposed paying rent on CRP land based on local cash rental rates with adjustment for each parcel.
Roberts said he hoped USDA would delay issuance of the rules because of his complaints they were biased against the Plains.
